explain.say: In 2019 an eighteen storey tower called Mjøstårnet opened in Norway, about eighty five metres tall and made mostly of wood. Timber is one of the oldest building materials and, suddenly, one of the most modern. Let us design something simpler: a floor joist four metres long, carrying three kilonewtons per metre.

explain.say: Wood is full of water. Moisture content is the weight of water over the weight of dry wood: a sample of six hundred grams that dries to five hundred holds twenty percent. Look at the graph. Wood only shrinks below about thirty percent, and twice as much across the rings as along the radius. Why should timber dry before it goes into a heated house?

explain.say: So it does not shrink and crack after it is built in! Timber is sorted into strength classes. C twenty four softwood has a bending strength of twenty four megapascals. A seventy five by two hundred millimetre joist has a section modulus of half a million cubic millimetres. After safety and moisture factors, it resists about seven point four kilonewton metres.

loads.label: 3 kN/m floor
loads.ask: How do you check a timber joist for bending?

explain.say: Now the demand. Look at the moment diagram: the joist sags most in the middle, where the bending moment peaks at w L squared over eight, three times sixteen over eight, six kilonewton metres. Six is less than seven point four, so it passes. Each support pushes up six kilonewtons. Would a five metre span still pass?

explain.say: No, the moment would jump to over nine! For big buildings, engineers glue boards in crossing layers to make cross-laminated timber, stiff in both directions. In a fire, thick timber chars on the outside, about two thirds of a millimetre a minute, and the char protects the core. Brilliant! faq.q: What is the moisture content of timber?
faq.a: The mass of water in the wood divided by the mass of the oven-dry wood, as a percentage. Six hundred grams drying to five hundred grams is 20 percent.
asks: How do you calculate the moisture content of timber?

faq.q: What is the fibre saturation point?
faq.a: The moisture content, about 25 to 30 percent, at which the cell walls are full of water but the cell cavities are empty. Timber only shrinks or swells, and changes strength, below it.
C24 is a softwood strength class with a characteristic bending strength of 24 megapascals. Higher numbers, like C30, are stronger; hardwoods use D classes.

faq.q: How do you check a timber joist for bending?
faq.a: Work out the maximum moment, w L squared over 8 for a simply supported joist, and compare it with the design strength times the section modulus. A 75 by 200 C24 joist resists about 7.4 kilonewton metres.

faq.a: CLT is made of layers of boards glued with the grain of each layer at right angles to the next, forming large, stiff panels used for walls and floors in tall timber buildings.

facts: Norway's Mjøstårnet, completed in 2019, is about 85 m tall and built largely of glued laminated timber and CLT.
Solid softwood chars at a rate of roughly 0.65 mm per minute in a standard fire.
